title: Modular Wheelchair Tray and Armrest Mount
summary: A tool-free, swing-away tray and height-adjustable armrest that clamps to most manual wheelchair frames without drilling.

cover.alt: Manual wheelchair fitted with a swing-away tray and adjustable armrest mount

problem: Wheelchair users at the partner clinic relied on fixed lap trays that blocked transfers and had to be removed by a caregiver. Commercial alternatives required frame drilling, voiding manufacturer warranties.
requirements: Clamp to round tubes from 22 to 28 mm without permanent modification
Swing clear of the user with one hand and limited grip strength
Support at least 20 kg distributed load with a safety factor of 2
Fit within the chair's folded envelope for car transport
approach: I mapped transfer motions with three users and their occupational therapist, then defined a pivot location that clears the knee during side transfers. Concepts were scored against grip effort, mass and adjustability.

process.title: Concept & user mapping
process.body: Sketched 12 clamp and pivot concepts; three progressed to foam-core and 3D-printed mock-ups tested with users.

process.title: Detailed design
process.body: Modelled the clamp in SolidWorks with a split-collar geometry and cam lever sized for a 15 N actuation force.

process.title: Analysis
process.body: Ran static FEA on the bracket under 2× rated load and iterated pocketing to remove mass while keeping peak stress under 120 MPa.

fabrication: Brackets were CNC milled from 6061-T6 aluminium and bead-blasted; the tray surface was laser-cut from 6 mm HDPE. I produced the drawings, tolerancing and assembly instructions for the lab technician.
outcome: Two units were deployed for a four-week trial. Users could stow the tray independently, and the clinic adopted the design as a reference for future adaptations.
